summary: Implemented the T064 robustness and anti-overfitting analysis. Added a new `robinhood_lp.robustness` package (8 modules, ~4000 lines) plus 1474-line test suite covering every T064 acceptance clause: anchored/rolling walk-forward splits (`WalkForwardSplit`), untouched time holdout (`TimeHoldoutSplit`), pool holdout as primary generalisation (`PoolHoldoutSplit` + per-held-out-pool results in the report), single purge/embargo gap derived from a `LabelHorizon` (hand-chosen lengths rejected at construction), machine-recorded point-in-time `SplitBoundary` records with deterministic IDs, a scenario catalogue covering the six T064 stress/failure categories with halt-or-degrade outcomes declared before the run (DS-035), a degradation policy that rejects undefined behaviour and forced trades (DS-041), parameter surfaces with deterministic cross-product enumeration, pool/regime segmentation that refuses post-hoc drops, and a multiple-comparison disclosure that reports sensitivity spread beside the best metric. The `RobustnessReport` separates train/validation/test as disjoint segment-label sets and refuses to publish without non-empty pool-holdout results. The `RobustnessRunner` reads the catalogue before any data is touched and assembles the report via injected fold/pool evaluators. 82 pytest tests pass; ruff format/check clean; strict mypy clean on the 9 new/changed files.

residual_risks: The robustness package is a self-contained analytical layer; it does not invoke the backtest engine or the strategy baselines itself. Integration with the research harness (T101) is out of scope here; a follow-up task will wire RobustnessRunner.run() to per-fold and per-pool engine invocations.

Two pre-existing test failures (test_abi_artifacts.py and test_documentation_citations.py) were observed in the full suite. They are unrelated to T064 and were present at base commit 41bda04; they should be addressed by their owning tasks.

The pool-holdout boundary records use the held-out pool's first block (block_range_start) as the anchor. Future revisions may want to also record the training pools' boundaries explicitly; the current shape leaves train-pool edges implicit via the fold_role=boundary record.

The default scenario catalogue (default_stress_scenario_catalogue) uses fixed severities (gas x10, latency +600, slippage +200bps, fee x0.5). These are reasonable first-cut defaults; a future task may want to drive them from a configurable profile per the run's actual cost / latency evidence.
The sensitivity summary currently reports the range (best - worst) as the spread. The acceptance clause allows range or stddev; stddev would be a larger refactor and is left for a future task.
